'''James Michael Ray McAdoo''' (born January 4, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Shimane Susanoo Magic]] of the [[B.League]] in Japan. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]], and twice earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). McAdoo won two [[NBA championship]]s with the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He has also played in various international leagues, including the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]], Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL), and [[ABA League]].

==High school career==
[[File:James Michael McAdoo Jordan Brand Classic.jpg|thumb|left|upright|McAdoo at the 2011 Jordan Brand Classic]]
Born and raised in [[Norfolk, Virginia]], McAdoo attended [[Norfolk Christian Schools|Norfolk Christian High School]]. As a junior in 2009–10, he averaged 22.5 points and 9.9 rebounds per game. As a senior in 2010–11, McAdoo averaged 21.6 points and 8.1 rebounds per game. He led Norfolk Christian to consecutive state championships and earned Gatorade Player of the Year honors in Virginia in 2010 and 2011. During his career, McAdoo earned USA Today first team and [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] third team honors, as well as earning co-Most Valuable Player honors at both the McDonald's All-America Game (17 points) in Chicago and the Jordan Brand Classic (26 points, 14 rebounds) in Charlotte.<ref name=bio>{{cite web |url=http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205497513 |title=James Michael McAdoo Bio |work=GoHeels.com |access-date=September 2, 2014 |archive-date=October 9, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141009080546/http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205497513 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In September 2009, McAdoo committed to the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://blogs.newsobserver.com/prepsnow/bob-mcadoos-nephew-commits-to-unc |title=Bob McAdoo's nephew commits to UNC |first=Ken |last=Tysiac |work=NewsObserver.com |date=September 7, 2009 |access-date=March 16, 2012  |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130320041136/http://blogs.newsobserver.com/prepsnow/bob-mcadoos-nephew-commits-to-unc |archive-date=March 20, 2013 }}</ref> After [[Travis Wear|Travis]] and [[David Wear]] transferred from UNC, McAdoo considered graduating a year early so he could join the Tar Heels in 2010, but McAdoo ultimately decided to stay at Norfolk Christian through his senior year.<ref name="familiar"/>

McAdoo was rated as the #4 player in the class of 2011 by [[Scout.com]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&cfg=bb&pid=88&yr=2011 |title=SCOUT.COM COLLEGE BASKETBALL TEAM RECRUITING PROSPECTS |work=Scout.com |access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref> the #6 player in the [[ESPNU]] 100,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/67008/james-mcadoo |title=James Michael McAdoo – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles – ESPN |work=ESPN.com |access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref> and the #8 player by [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2288 |title=Yahoo Sports: Rivals.com Ranking – Rivals150 for the class of 2011 |work=Yahoo.com |access-date=August 26, 2010}}</ref>

==College career==
McAdoo played three seasons at the University of North Carolina, recording career averages of 11.4 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.0 assists, and 1.2 steals in 25.0 minutes over 108 games. As a junior in 2013–14, he earned All-ACC second team honors for the second straight year after averaging 14.2 points, 6.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.3 steals in 34 games.<ref name="bio"/>

On April 3, 2014, McAdoo declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zimmerman|first=Kevin|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/4/3/5578814/2014-nba-draft-north-carolina-james-michael-mcadoo |title=2014 NBA Draft: North Carolina's James Michael McAdoo declares |work=SBNation.com |date=April 3, 2014 |access-date=April 3, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Golden State Warriors (2014–2017)===
After going undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]], McAdoo joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Announce 2014 Summer League Roster & T.V. Schedule|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-announce-2014-summer-league-roster-t.v.-schedule|access-date=July 3, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 3, 2014}}</ref> On September 2, 2014, he signed with the Warriors,<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Sign Aaron Craft, James Michael Mcadoo & Mitchell Watt to Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/craft-mcadoo-watt-20140902|access-date=September 2, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=September 2, 2014}}</ref> but was later waived by the team on October 24.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Waive Craft, Kapono, Kilpatrick, Mcadoo and Watt|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/five-players-waived-20141024|access-date=October 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2014}}</ref> On November 3, McAdoo was acquired by the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] as an affiliate player of Golden State.<ref>{{cite news|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2014 Training Camp Roster|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_training_camp_roster_110314.html|access-date=November 11, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141109024823/http://www.nba.com/dleague/santacruz/warriors_training_camp_roster_110314.html|archive-date=November 9, 2014}}</ref>

On January 19, 2015, McAdoo signed a 10-day contract with the Golden State Warriors.<ref name="c430">{{cite web | last=Fahey | first=Andy | title=Warriors Sign James Michael McAdoo to 10-Day Contract | website=NBA.com | date=2015-01-19 | url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/mcadoo-signing-20150119 | access-date=2025-03-10}}</ref> He made his NBA debut later that night as McAdoo came off the bench to record 11 points and five rebounds in the 122–79 victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150119/DENGSW/gameinfo.html |title=Warriors whip Nuggets 122-79 for season's most lopsided win |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 20, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150120055950/http://www.nba.com/games/20150119/DENGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 20, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was not retained by Golden State following the expiration of his contract on January 29,<ref>[https://www.santacruzsentinel.com/sports/20150129/d-league-basketball-santa-cruz-warriors-roster-bolstered-by-nba-talent D-League basketball: Santa Cruz Warrior's roster bolstered by NBA talent]</ref> and McAdoo returned to Santa Cruz the following day.<ref>[http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150130/SCWRNO/ Williams, Warriors Edge Bighorns]</ref> On February 2, he returned to Golden State, signing a second 10-day contract with the team.<ref>[https://www.nba.com/warriors/warriors-sign-james-michael-mcadoo-second-10-day-contract Warriors Sign James Michael McAdoo To Second 10-Day Contract]</ref> Following the expiration of his second 10-day contract, McAdoo returned to Santa Cruz where he played two games before being called up again by Golden State on February 19, signing with the team for the rest of the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/mcadoo-signing-20150219 Warriors Sign James Michael McAdoo for Remainder of the Season]</ref> He was assigned multiple times to Santa Cruz to finish the season,<ref>{{cite news|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|access-date=July 24, 2016|work=NBA.com|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref> as McAdoo earned NBA D-League All-Rookie first team and All-NBA D-League second team honors.<ref>{{cite news|title=NBA Development League Announces 2014-15 All-League Teams|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-announces-2014-15-all-league-teams/|access-date=April 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=April 22, 2015|archive-date=April 26, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150426012519/http://dleague.nba.com/news/nba-development-league-announces-2014-15-all-league-teams/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went on to win a D-League championship with Santa Cruz<ref>{{cite news|title=Title Wave: Santa Cruz Wins NBA D-League Championship|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20150426/FWNSCW/|access-date=April 26, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=April 26, 2015}}</ref> and an NBA championship with Golden State; McAdoo appeared in just over a minute of action for the Warriors during the [[2015 NBA Finals]] against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/mcadoja01/gamelog/2015/ James Michael McAdoo 2014-15 Game Log]</ref>

McAdoo retained his spot on Golden State's roster for the 2015–16 season, but missed all of January and February due to a sprained toe on his left foot.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors ride hot shooting to 115-112 victory over Clippers|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/GSWLAC/gameinfo.html|access-date=February 21, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229100226/http://www.nba.com/games/20160220/GSWLAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 29, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 21, 2016, McAdoo made his first NBA start, recording seven points and six rebounds in 17½ minutes of action in a 109–104 victory over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Green, Warriors nip Timberwolves, 109-104|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20160321/GSWMIN/gameinfo.html|access-date=March 22, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=March 21, 2016}}</ref> The Warriors returned to the [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] in 2016, where they were defeated in seven games by the Cavaliers despite a 3–1 lead.

On July 13, 2016, McAdoo re-signed with the Warriors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Warriors Re-Sign Free Agent Forward James Michael McAdoo|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-mcadoo-20160713|access-date=July 13, 2016|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2016}}</ref> The Warriors won 67 games in the 2016–17 season and made their way through to their third straight [[2017 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. There, the Warriors defeated the Cavaliers in five games to claim their second championship in three years. The Warriors finished the playoffs with a 16–1 record, the best postseason winning percentage in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 14, 2017 |title=Warriors (16–1) Record Best Postseason Winning Percentage in NBA History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2715556-warriors-16-1-record-best-postseason-winning-percentage-in-nba-history |access-date=May 10, 2018 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2017–2018)===
On August 30, 2017, McAdoo signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-mcadoo-blackmon-jr|title=Sixers Sign McAdoo, Blackmon Jr.|work=NBA.com|date=August 30, 2017|access-date=August 30, 2017}}</ref> Under the terms of the deal, he spent the majority of the 2017–18 season with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]]. On January 15, 2018, McAdoo was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/jackson-signed-two-way-contract|title=Jackson Signed to Two-Way Contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 15, 2018|access-date=January 15, 2018}}</ref>

===Agua Caliente Clippers (2018)===
On January 25, 2018, McAdoo was reacquired by the Delaware 87ers. The next day, he was traded to the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] in exchange for a 2018 first-round draft pick and the returning player rights to [[Corey Hawkins (basketball)|Corey Hawkins]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://delaware.gleague.nba.com/news/delaware-87ers-acquire-2018-first-round-pick-returning-player-rights-corey-hawkins/|title=DELAWARE 87ERS ACQUIRE 2018 FIRST-ROUND PICK AND RETURNING PLAYER RIGHTS TO COREY HAWKINS|work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2018|access-date=January 28, 2018|archive-date=January 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126210918/http://delaware.gleague.nba.com/news/delaware-87ers-acquire-2018-first-round-pick-returning-player-rights-corey-hawkins/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Auxilium Torino (2018–2019)===
On July 15, 2018, McAdoo signed with Italian club [[Auxilium Torino]] for [[2018–19 LBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/281880/james-michael-mcadoo-signs-with-fiat-torino.html|title=James Michael McAdoo signs with Fiat Torino|work=Sportando.basketball|date=July 15, 2018|access-date=July 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715152009/https://sportando.basketball/en/italy/serie-a/281880/james-michael-mcadoo-signs-with-fiat-torino.html|archive-date=July 15, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Beşiktaş (2019–2020) ===
On August 1, 2019, McAdoo signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş Sompo Japan]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/besiktas-signs-james-michael-mcadoo/|title=Besiktas signs James Michael McAdoo|date=August 1, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 7, 2019|last1=Carchia|first1=Emiliano|archive-date=August 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801155020/https://sportando.basketball/en/besiktas-signs-james-michael-mcadoo/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Partizan (2020) ===
On January 7, 2020, McAdoo signed with [[KK Partizan]] of the [[ABA League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=McAdoo, Besiktas officially part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/mcadoo-besiktas-officially-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=January 7, 2020 |date=January 7, 2020 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano |archive-date=January 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115002647/https://sportando.basketball/en/mcadoo-besiktas-officially-part-ways/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Sun Rockers Shibuya (2020–2024)===
On July 2, 2020, McAdoo signed with the [[Sun Rockers Shibuya]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Hughes | first=Grant | title=Ex-UNC Star James Michael McAdoo Signs With New Team | website=247Sports | date=2020-07-02 | url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/Article/UNC-James-Michael-McAdoo-Signs-With-Japans-Sun-Rockers-Shibuya-148765488/ | access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref>

==National team career==
McAdoo averaged 16.8 points, 8.6 rebounds and 2.0 blocks to help Team USA win the gold medal at the 2009 [[FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]], played in Argentina. He was subsequently named the 2009 USA Basketball Male Athlete of the Year.<ref name="bio" /> In 2010, McAdoo won another gold medal after averaging 14.5 points, 7.9 rebounds and 1.9 blocks at the [[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]], in Germany. He was [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|named to the All-Tournament Team]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Barbour|first=Brian|url=https://www.tarheelblog.com/2010/07/james-mcadoo-wins-gold-heels-offer-cody-zeller |title=James McAdoo Wins Gold; Heels Offer Cody Zeller |work=tarheelblog.com |date=July 11, 2010 |access-date=July 11, 2010}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McAdoo is an [[Evangelicalism|Evangelical Christian]]. He has spoken about his faith saying, "I just want people to realize I don’t play basketball for myself. No matter what adversities I face, how bad a season goes, or even how good a season goes, at the end of the day I’m playing for a bigger reason, and that’s to glorify my Lord and Savior [[Jesus|Jesus Christ]]."<ref>{{cite web|last=Rennicke|first=Sarah|title=Anchored in the Whirlwind|url=https://www.fca.org/2014/06/26/anchored-in-the-whirlwind|work=fca.org|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=June 26, 2014}}</ref>

McAdoo's parents, Ronnie and Janet, both played basketball at [[Old Dominion Monarchs basketball|Old Dominion]] in the late 1970s and the early 80s, and went on to play professionally in [[Europe]], while his older sister Kelsey also played basketball at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte.<ref name="fay">{{cite news|url=http://www.fayobserver.com/opinion/article_af8392e6-a56c-53b1-88d5-99b456efb1a7.html|title=Live Wire: Basketball talent runs in McAdoo family|first=Catherine|last=Pritchard|work=FayObserver.com|date=June 17, 2011|access-date=March 16, 2012}}</ref> Ronnie McAdoo is the second cousin of [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] basketball player [[Bob McAdoo]], who played at North Carolina and in the NBA.<ref name="familiar">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/2011/06/26/1301563/mcadoo-following-in-his-uncles.html|title=McAdoo following familiar footsteps to UNC|first=Robbi|last=Pickeral|work=Raleigh News and Observer|date=June 26, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110808042654/http://www.newsobserver.com/2011/06/26/1301563/mcadoo-following-in-his-uncles.html|archive-date=August 8, 2011|access-date=March 16, 2012}}</ref> McAdoo said that he calls Bob "uncle" although he does not know what their exact relationship is, and that "My dad's great-great-great grandfather and [Bob's] great-grandfather are like brothers."<ref name="fay"/><!--If they are brothers, then he is 2nd cousin once removed. Not sure what "like brothers" means.-->

"James Michael" is McAdoo's first name.<ref name=brown>{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=C.L. |title=McAdoo playing with purpose |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/89998/mcadoo-playing-with-purpose |website=ESPN |access-date=July 26, 2025 |date=November 15, 2013}}</ref> He is named after his father's three best friends who died young: brothers James and Michael McPherson, and Old Dominion teammate Ray Broxton.<ref name=brown/> McAdoo was known as James McAdoo during his high school career but he requested that his full first name be used before he arrived at North Carolina.<ref name=brown/>

On April 2, 2014, McAdoo married Lauren Elizabeth Adkins, a UNC volleyball player.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dailytarheel.com/article/2014/06/qa-with-former-unc-forward-james-michael-mcadoo|title=Q&A with former UNC forward James Michael McAdoo|first=Aaron|last=Dodson|work=DailyTarHeel.com|date=June 19, 2014|access-date=June 19, 2014}}</ref>

In November of 2022, McAdoo started the Better Blue Podcast with former NBA player and Duke Blue Devil [[Ryan Kelly (basketball)|Ryan Kelly]] in which they recount their own college memories and the current state of the [[NCAA]], especially their thoughts on their alma mater teams, [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|UNC]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/@betterbluepodcast | title=The Better Blue Podcast | website=[[YouTube]] }}</ref>
